source: Design a multiplayer puzzle-strategy game where players have a 3D grid in their base. Base items drop regularly or can be purchased; combining two identical items (e.g., two Level 1 swords) merges them into a higher-level item (a Level 2 sword). The goal is to develop your base's economy and fend off waves of monsters using your most powerful merged equipment.

answers.ask: Swords and monsters suggest fantasy - is that right, or is this sci-fi or modern?
answers.answer: Yes, use a straightforward high-fantasy theme: swords, monsters, and fantasy-style base equipment.

answers.ask: How many players share a session, and does each get their own base plot?
answers.answer: Support a small session of up to 8 players, with each player receiving their own separate base plot and 3D grid.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] theme — Q: Swords and monsters suggest fantasy - is that right, or is this sci-fi or modern? A: Yes, use a straightforward high-fantasy theme: swords, monsters, and fantasy-style base equipment.
- [author] scale — Q: How many players share a session, and does each get their own base plot? A: Support a small session of up to 8 players, with each player receiving their own separate base plot and 3D grid.
- [agent_inferred] plot and grid arrangement — Q: How should eight unspecified grids be sized and arranged? A: Use eight isolated plots in two rows of four, each containing a compact 4x4 item grid.
- [agent_inferred] wave origins — Q: Do monsters share one origin or attack each plot independently? A: Give each base one wave origin outside its plot so all eight plots remain independently playable.

## Enriched image prompt
Create a high-fantasy multiplayer base field with exactly eight separate, equally spaced player plots arranged in two rows of four. Each plot contains one defensible fantasy core and one compact raised 4x4 grid of 16 clearly separated cells for swords and other mergeable equipment, with open placement access around it. Outside each plot, provide one monster approach facing the core while keeping neighbouring plots from overlapping. Use straightforward fantasy stone, timber, banners, and weapon-display forms, and frame all eight independent bases in one readable plan.

## Genre
The dominant genre is Strategy because players develop bases and defend them from monster waves; Puzzle is secondary because identical equipment is combined on a grid.

## Shape and preset
Use `plot-isolated`, taken from outside Strategy's usual shape set, because up to eight players each require an independent non-overlapping base. Preset is none: available defense presets assume shared open terrain or a fixed lane rather than eight merge-grid plots.

## Config requirements
`tile-grid` draws one 4x4 three-dimensional equipment grid in each of the eight plots, for exactly 128 cells overall. `tracker-core` draws one fantasy base core behind each grid, for exactly eight cores. Plot boundaries, approach ground, and equipment-scaled cells remain visually distinct.

## Layout requirements
Place `tracker-core` once in every plot, centered behind its grid. Place `spawner-npc` exactly eight times, one monster-wave origin outside and facing each corresponding base. Mark all 128 grid cells as free-text BuildZone item-drop, purchase-arrival, and merge positions, while ensuring a spawned item uses an empty cell. Place one free-text SpawnZone within each plot for up to eight total players.

## Layout components
The map contains exactly eight isolated plots, eight 4x4 grids, 128 grid cells, eight base cores, eight player arrivals, and eight monster origins. Each plot has clear space around its grid and a direct open approach from its origin to its core. Equal spacing prevents overlap, and the two-by-four composition keeps every base readable in one frame.

## Render order
Use `topdown`: the eight equal plots, all 4x4 grids, and one-to-one wave approaches must be authoritative before fantasy dressing is added.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
The scale band is large because eight independent player plots must coexist without overlap. The theme is straightforward high fantasy with swords, monsters, and base equipment. `P0` is sufficient because all plots occupy one grounded surface with no fixed enemy lane, interior transition, or stacked play.
